cover.title: Multimodal Affect Recognition for Unseen Visitors in a Free-Roaming VR Museum
cover.author: Akshaj Somanpura Rajendran

Abinaya2026.label: Abinaya and Dinakaran, 2026
Abinaya2026.full: Abinaya, G. and Dinakaran, K. (2026). Adaptive multimodal learning for driver cognitive state monitoring using transformer-based fusion with personalized meta-learning and federated optimization. Scientific Reports. DOI 10.1038/s41598-026-51635-3.
Abinaya2026.note: Repaired. A single unedited in-press study of 21 drivers cannot establish what the literature identifies as reliably lifting cross-person accuracy. The Discussion sentence now reports what the paper reports, that per-user calibration has been found to lift it.
Abinaya2026.says: Under subject-independent 5-fold cross-validation, AML achieves 80.5 ± 1.8% accuracy on binary cognitive load classification without personalization, rising to 91.8 ± 1.2% with K = 20 calibration samples (~40 s). Under the more rigorous leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) protocol, AML reaches 77.8 ± 2.6% without personalization and 84.0 ± 1.8% with K = 20 personalization.

Andrew2013.label: Andrew et al., 2013
Andrew2013.full: Andrew, G., Arora, R., Bilmes, J., and Livescu, K. (2013). Deep canonical correlation analysis. Proceedings of the 30th International Conference on Machine Learning.
Andrew2013.note: The paper establishes exactly what the current thesis text attributes to it. Use 1 (§Aligning Asynchronous Modalities, l.155): 'learns such features too' — supported ('simultaneously learns two deep nonlinear mappings of two views that are maximally correlated'); 'performs no warping' — supported by absence: warping, alignment and DTW appear nowhere in the paper, the objective is purely corr(f1(X1),f2(X2)); 'requires the two views to arrive as paired observations, one column of each matched to one of the other, since its objective is built on the cross-covariance' — supported verbatim by the H1, H2 ∈ R^{o×m} column definition and Σ̂12 = 1/(m−1) H̄1 H̄02; 'The original work obtains that pairing by downsampling the faster view' — supported verbatim by the XRMB setup; 'defined for two views only' — supported, the method is two-view throughout. Use 2 (§Alignment Method Comparison, l.365): 'adds learned correlated projections' — supported, DCCA is precisely learned projections maximising correlation. The one clause not sourced from this paper is 'it is the special case of DCTW with the warping fixed to the identity', which is a statement about Trigeorgis2016 and is only negatively supported here (Andrew2013 predates DCTW). The prior WRONG verdict was written against an earlier wording ('needs both signals already sampled at the same rate', 'has to be applied after a windowing step') that no longer exists in the file — those phrases are gone and the replacement text is accurate. No repair needed.
Andrew2013.says: In this work we introduce deep CCA (DCCA), which simultaneously learns two deep nonlinear mappings of two views that are maximally correlated. ... Let H1 ∈ Ro×m , H2 ∈ Ro×m be matrices whose columns are the top-level representations produced by the deep models on the two views, for a training set of size m. ... The articulatory measurements are downsampled to match the MFCC frame rate.

Baevski2020.label: Baevski et al., 2020
Baevski2020.full: Baevski, A., Zhou, H., Mohamed, A., and Auli, M. (2020). wav2vec 2.0: A framework for self-supervised learning of speech representations. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems.
Baevski2020.note: Baevski2020 [3] §2.3 speech para Self-supervised embeddings are more powerful but pre-trained on far larger corpora than an affect study supplies Self-supervised speech representation learning; large unlabelled pre-training then fine-tuning on little labelled data. The powerful-but-data-hungry alternative to GeMAPS. OK (after correction) indirect (SSL review) + fulltext of companion keys, 2026-09-02

Bruder2024.label: Bruder et al., 2024
Bruder2024.full: Bruder, C., Poeppel, D., and Larrouy-Maestri, P. (2024). Perceptual (but not acoustic) features predict singing voice preferences. Scientific Reports, 14.
Bruder2024.note: Both uses check out: Krippendorff's alpha for liking was 0.10 (0.07 on raw ratings), i.e. agreement-based rather than variance-partitioned, while mean liking ratings correlated highly between the US online and German lab cohorts, matching 'low agreement even where average preferences were stable across cohorts'. Different domain (singing-voice aesthetics, not affect) but it is used only as a parallel, which is fair.
Bruder2024.says: Inter-rater agreement in liking and perceptual ratings was low, indicating substantial (and unsurprising) individual differences in participants' preferences and perception of the stimuli.

Doewes2023.label: Doewes et al., 2023
Doewes2023.full: Doewes, A., Kurdhi, N. A., and Saxena, A. (2023). Evaluating quadratic weighted kappa as the standard performance metric for automated essay scoring. Proceedings of the 16th International Conference on Educational Data Mining (EDM). DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8115784.
Doewes2023.note: Read the local PDF text. The paper states exactly the two properties the thesis attributes to it - sensitivity to the range of scores ('its value varying significantly in response to changes in the range of scores') and sensitivity to prevalence/imbalanced agreement - and its explicit conclusion is that QWK should not be the sole metric. Different task (automated essay scoring), but the claim is about the metric itself, so the fit is fine.
Doewes2023.says: However, we have identified several limitations of using QWK as the sole metric for evaluating AES model performance. These limitations include its sensitivity to the rating scale, the potential for the so-called "kappa paradox" to occur, the impact of prevalence, the impact of the position of agreements in the diagonal agreement matrix, and its limitation in handling a large number of raters.

Eyben2016.label: Eyben et al., 2016
Eyben2016.full: Eyben, F., Scherer, K. R., Schuller, B. W., Sundberg, J., André, E., Busso, C., Devillers, L. Y., Epps, J., Laukka, P., Narayanan, S. S., and Truong, K. P. (2016). The Geneva Minimalistic Acoustic Parameter Set (GeMAPS) for voice research and affective computing. IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing, 7(2), 190--202.
Eyben2016.note: Eyben2016 [6] §2.3 speech para GeMAPS is 62 parameters with an 88-parameter extension; its minimalism guards against over-adapting to small corpora Defines the GeMAPS and eGeMAPS acoustic parameter sets. The acoustic feature set, its size, and the small-data rationale. Now also carries the prosody claim that ElAyadi2011 held. OK fulltext, 2026-09-01

FEEL2025.label: Singh et al., 2025
FEEL2025.full: Singh, P., Gupta, A., Jalan, S., Kumar, M., and Singh, P. (2025). FEEL: Quantifying heterogeneity in physiological signals for generalizable emotion recognition. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS), Datasets and Benchmarks Track. arXiv:2604.05926.
FEEL2025.note: Repaired in both sentences. 'the deep alternatives fail' contradicted the paper, whose best-performing family is itself a pretrained deep model; it now reads 'networks trained end-to-end on raw signal fail'. 'nineteen wearable datasets' is now 'nineteen physiological datasets', since not all nineteen are wrist-recorded.
FEEL2025.says: We introduce FEEL (Framework for Emotion Evaluation), the first large-scale benchmarking study of emotion recognition using electrodermal activity (EDA) and photoplethysmography (PPG) signals across 19 publicly available datasets. [...] Models leveraging handcrafted features (107/114) consistently outperform those trained on raw signal segments, underscoring the value of domain knowledge in low-resource, noisy settings. [...] We evaluated the performance of our ML and DL models using Leave-One-Subject-Out Cross-Validation (LOSO-CV), to ensure subject-independent evaluation and reflect real-world deployment conditions. [...] emotion recognition from physiological signals faces ongoing challenges, including increased signal noise, environmental variability, high inter-subject variability, and a lack of large-scale, standardized datasets [...] Within the deep learning category, the handcrafted feature-based MLP achieved 11 top results, while signal-based deep models accounted for 3, and handcrafted features combined with attention mechanisms contributed 2 best-performing instances. [...] fine-tuned contrastive signal-language pretraining (CLSP) models (71/114) achieve the highest F1 across arousal and valence classification tasks

Hutto2014.label: Hutto and Gilbert, 2014
Hutto2014.full: Hutto, C. J. and Gilbert, E. (2014). VADER: A parsimonious rule-based model for sentiment analysis of social media text. Proceedings of the Eighth International AAAI Conference on Weblogs and Social Media (ICWSM-14), 216--225.
Hutto2014.note: Hutto2014 [8] §2.3 speech para Lexicon-based scoring gives a training-free estimate of valence per utterance Lexicon-and-rules sentiment model, validated on short informal social-media text. The training-free valence estimate for transcribed speech. OK (after narrowing) fulltext, 2026-09-01

Makowski2021.label: Makowski et al., 2021
Makowski2021.full: Makowski, D., Pham, T., Lau, Z. J., Brammer, J. C., Lespinasse, F., Pham, H., Schölzel, C., and Chen, S. H. A. (2021). NeuroKit2: A Python toolbox for neurophysiological signal processing. Behavior Research Methods, 53, 1689--1696.
Makowski2021.note: Checked the local PDF text: it is a software paper covering EDA processing and citing cvxEDA and Ledalab as the model-based skin-conductance decomposition methods it wraps, so it is the right tool citation for 'decomposed into tonic and phasic parts with NeuroKit2'. The 0.01-5 Hz band and motion correction in the same sentence are van der Kaaden's choices, not NeuroKit2 claims, and the sentence already attributes them elsewhere.
Makowski2021.says: It provides a comprehensive suite of processing routines for a variety of bodily signals (e.g., ECG, PPG, EDA, EMG, RSP).

Radford2022.label: Radford et al., 2023
Radford2022.full: Radford, A., Kim, J. W., Xu, T., Brockman, G., McLeavey, C., and Sutskever, I. (2023). Robust speech recognition via large-scale weak supervision. Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 202, 28492--28518.
Radford2022.note: Checked the local PDF; the citation only carries the clause 'once speech has been transcribed automatically', and Whisper is a robust zero-shot ASR system, so the attribution is correct and minimal. The affect claim in the same sentence rests on Hutto2014, not this paper.
Radford2022.says: When scaled to 680,000 hours of multilingual and multitask supervision, the resulting models generalize well to standard benchmarks and are often competitive with prior fully supervised results but in a zero-shot transfer setting without the need for any fine-tuning.

XueRCEA2021.label: Xue et al., 2021b
XueRCEA2021.full: Xue, T., El Ali, A., Zhang, T., Ding, G., and Cesar, P. (2021). RCEA-360VR: Real-time, continuous emotion annotation in 360$^$ VR videos for collecting precise viewport-dependent ground truth labels. In Proceedings of the 2021 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, CHI '21. ACM. DOI 10.1145/3411764.3445487.
XueRCEA2021.note: Repaired. The claim that peaks were detected 'following the RCEA-360VR approach' is gone; that paper aligns annotations by dynamic time warping against video colour features and contains no feature peak detection. Its remaining use, real-time joystick annotation over the valence-arousal plane in VR, is exactly what it describes.
XueRCEA2021.says: The movement of the joystick head maps into a 2D V-A space, where the x axis indicates valence, while the y axis indicates arousal ... Dynamic time warping (DTW) ... is used to calculate similarity between S_Pij and CFi. We get the shifted sequence with the highest similarity and the corresponding tau is recorded as the annotation time delay.

Yang2021.label: Yang et al., 2021
Yang2021.full: Yang, S., Chi, P., Chuang, Y., Lai, C., Lakhotia, K., Lin, Y. Y., Liu, A. T., Shi, J., Chang, X., Lin, G., Huang, T., Tseng, W., Lee, K., Liu, D., Huang, Z., Dong, S., Li, S., Watanabe, S., Mohamed, A., and Lee, H. (2021). SUPERB: Speech processing Universal PERformance Benchmark. Proceedings of Interspeech 2021.
Yang2021.note: Checked the results table: on the Emotion Recognition task FBANK scores 35.39% accuracy against 63.43% for wav2vec 2.0 Base and 67.62% for HuBERT Large, which supports the claim for wav2vec2 and for emotion recognition specifically. SUPERB predates WavLM and does not evaluate it, but the sentence co-cites Chen2022WavLM, so that half is covered.
Yang2021.says: For the tasks using linear models, FBANK cannot work on any task, while SSL representations all perform well to some degree with different specializations... Their results on SID and ER are also highly competitive.

Chen2016XGBoost.label: Chen and Guestrin, 2016
Chen2016XGBoost.full: Chen, T. and Guestrin, C. (2016). XGBoost: A scalable tree boosting system. Proceedings of the 22nd ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining.
Chen2016XGBoost.note: Verified the abstract via OpenAlex (DOI 10.1145/2939672.2939785); this is the XGBoost system paper and the thesis cites it only as the source of XGBoost as a realisation of gradient-boosted trees, which is exactly what it is. Good fit for a tabular tree-ensemble thesis.
Chen2016XGBoost.says: In this paper, we describe a scalable end-to-end tree boosting system called XGBoost, which is used widely by data scientists to achieve state-of-the-art results on many machine learning challenges.

Barrett2006.label: Barrett, 2006
Barrett2006.full: Barrett, L. F. (2006). Are emotions natural kinds? Perspectives on Psychological Science.
Barrett2006.note: Repaired. The paper argues emotion categories are not natural kinds and reports individual differences in them, but makes no psychometric claim about shared scales or a common zero. The sentence is split so the citation sits only on the category half.
Barrett2006.says: In this article, I review the accumulating empirical evidence that is inconsistent with the view that there are kinds of emotion with boundaries that are carved in nature.

Batini2009.label: Batini et al., 2009
Batini2009.full: Batini, C., Cappiello, C., Francalanci, C., and Maurino, A. (2009). Methodologies for data quality assessment and improvement. ACM Computing Surveys, 41(3), 1--52. DOI 10.1145/1541880.1541883.
Batini2009.note: Verified the DOI through Crossref and read the survey PDF: it explicitly names accuracy, completeness and consistency as the basic dimensions, and later reports that consensus on metrics is highest for exactly those three, so the thesis sentence is a fair summary.
Batini2009.says: By analyzing these classifications, it is possible to define a basic set of data quality dimensions, including accuracy, completeness, consistency, and timeliness, which constitute the focus of the majority of authors.

Boucsein2012.label: Boucsein, 2012
Boucsein2012.full: Boucsein, W. (2012). Electrodermal Activity. Springer Science \& Business Media.
Boucsein2012.note: No local copy and the book text is paywalled (Springer redirected to login, Google Books API returned 429); the quotation above is the publisher's own description of this edition, which confirms the sweat-gland part, and the sympathetic-control part is the canonical content of this reference and is co-cited with Kreibig2010. Claim is standard and safe, but note that verification here is from the publisher description rather than the book's own pages.
Boucsein2012.says: Electrodermal activity — the activation of sweat glands in the skin in response to stress or other stimuli.

Bradley2008.label: Bradley et al., 2008
Bradley2008.full: Bradley, M. M., Miccoli, L., Escrig, M. A., and Lang, P. J. (2008). The pupil as a measure of emotional arousal and autonomic activation. Psychophysiology, 45(4):602--607.
Bradley2008.note: Both halves of the citing sentence are in the abstract verbatim: the covariation of pupillary change with skin conductance change during affective picture viewing, and the reading of both as sympathetic activation. The abstract adds that dilation follows arousal regardless of valence, which the thesis does not claim here. Checked against the PubMed Central copy of the published abstract.
Bradley2008.says: Pupillary changes during picture viewing covaried with skin conductance change, supporting the interpretation that sympathetic nervous system activity modulates these changes in the context of affective picture viewing. Taken together, the data provide strong support for the hypothesis that the pupil's response during affective picture viewing reflects emotional arousal associated with increased sympathetic activity.

Demscar2006.label: Demšar, 2006
Demscar2006.full: Demšar, J. (2006). Statistical comparisons of classifiers over multiple data sets. Journal of Machine Learning Research.
Demscar2006.note: Demsar does recommend the Wilcoxon signed-rank test for comparing two classifiers, and gives the reasons the thesis relies on (no normality assumption, robust to outlying per-unit differences). The only stretch is that his unit of replication is data sets, not participants within one dataset; the substitution is standard in LOSO work but is the thesis's own move, not his.
Demscar2006.says: Based on that, we recommend a set of simple, yet safe and robust non-parametric tests for statistical comparisons of classifiers: the Wilcoxon signed ranks test for comparison of two classifiers and the Friedman test with the corresponding post-hoc tests for comparison of more classifiers over multiple data sets.

Greco2016.label: Greco et al., 2016
Greco2016.full: Greco, A., Valenza, G., Lanatà, A., Scilingo, E. P., and Citi, L. (2016). cvxEDA: A convex optimization approach to electrodermal activity processing. IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering.
Greco2016.note: Greco2016 [21] §2.3 EDA para A convex-optimisation formulation recovers tonic and phasic components without a filter split Bayesian MAP convex-optimisation decomposition of EDA with a B-spline tonic and Bateman-function phasic response. The non-filter decomposition alternative, and the 0.05 Hz tonic assumption. OK (after correction) fulltext, 2026-09-01

Healey2005.label: Healey and Picard, 2005
Healey2005.full: Healey, J. A. and Picard, R. W. (2005). Detecting stress during real-world driving tasks using physiological sensors. IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems.
Healey2005.note: Found the paper at literature/downloaded_by_author/05.healey-picard.txt; the abstract and Section VI both give three stress levels recognised at 97.4% over five-minute intervals, so 'separating three levels of driver stress during real-world driving' is exact. Different task and sensor set (chest ECG, EMG, respiration, hand EDA) from the thesis, but it is cited only for the general point that EDA works outside the lab.
Healey2005.says: three levels of driver stress with an accuracy of over 97% across multiple drivers and driving days

HayesPetrov2015.label: Hayes and Petrov, 2016
HayesPetrov2015.full: Hayes, T. R. and Petrov, A. A. (2016). Mapping and correcting the influence of gaze position on pupil size measurements. Behavior Research Methods, 48(2):510--527.
HayesPetrov2015.note: Added to the bibliography today, having been on disk but uncited. Checked against the full local text. It carries the two things the sentence now claims: that gaze position accounts for 9 to 20 per cent of measured pupil variance, and that correcting for it is achievable. It does not carry the regress-and-keep-the-residual method itself, which is prior work the paper describes; Hayes and Petrov's own correction is a geometric model fitted to an artificial eye. The sentence therefore states the regression as this thesis's own choice.
HayesPetrov2015.says: A linear regression model using X and Y gaze coordinates as predictors was able to explain between 9 % and 20 % of the pupil variance depending on the system and the maximum visual angle. ... Thus, very accurate PFE correction is possible and the corrected pupillometric data have the precision necessary to measure typical cognitive effects without limiting the types of tasks that can be studied.

Koelstra2012.label: Koelstra et al., 2012
Koelstra2012.full: Koelstra, S., Muhl, C., Soleymani, M., Lee, J.-S., Yazdani, A., Ebrahimi, T., Pun, T., Nijholt, A., and Patras, I. (2012). DEAP: A database for emotion analysis using physiological signals. IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing.
Koelstra2012.note: Koelstra2012 Intro §1.2 DEAP is a standard dataset relying on clean, synchronised data unlike a real visit Koelstra et al. (2012), IEEE TAC . "The experiments were performed in two laboratory rooms"; participants "were seated approximately 1 meter from the screen." OK fulltext, 2026-09-01

Kret2019.label: Kret and Sjak-Shie, 2019
Kret2019.full: Kret, M. E. and Sjak-Shie, E. E. (2019). Preprocessing pupil size data: Guidelines and code. Behavior Research Methods.
Kret2019.note: Repaired. The gaze-angle correction was credited to this guideline, which names gaze position as a confound but calls correcting for it a limitation of its own pipeline. That sentence now cites HayesPetrov2015, whose method it is. The two remaining uses, the 1.5 to 9.0 mm plausible range and the general preprocessing pointer, are the paper's own.
Kret2019.says: As such, this manifestation of gaze position in pupil size should ideally be controlled or corrected for, which we acknowledge as a current limitation of our preprocessing pipeline and the provided code's functionality.

Kreibig2010.label: Kreibig, 2010
Kreibig2010.full: Kreibig, S. D. (2010). Autonomic nervous system activity in emotion: A review. Biological Psychology.
Kreibig2010.note: The PDF is not at the recorded path but a copy exists locally at literature/downloaded_by_author/Autonomic_Nervous_System_Activity_in_Emotion_A_Rev.txt; the review repeatedly ties electrodermal measures (SCL, SCR, nSRR) to sympathetic innervation of the eccrine sweat glands, supporting the clause it is attached to. The trailing 'can be recorded without clinical equipment' is not Kreibig's claim, but the cite sits on the first clause.
Kreibig2010.says: Reports furthermore indicate increased electrodermal activity ... additionally implicating sympathetic effects at the eccrine sweat glands, an effect which is cholinergically mediated.

Kumar2025.label: Kumar et al., 2025
Kumar2025.full: Kumar, M. J. D., Sukesh Rao, M., and Narendra, K. C. (2025). Multimodal emotion recognition: A comprehensive survey of datasets, methods, and applications. IEEE Access.
Kumar2025.note: The batch record said no copy on disk, but the paper is present as literature/downloaded_by_author/Multimodal_Emotion_Recognition_A_Comprehensive_Survey_of_Datasets_Methods_and_Applications.txt (IEEE Access, Dileep Kumar, Sukesh Rao, Narendra — the right paper), so this was judged on the full text, not an abstract. All three uses hold. Use 1 (§Research Gap, l.29) 'typically studied in laboratory settings, with the field only recently shifting toward real-world, continuous monitoring' — supported almost word for word by the abstract and by the body's 'the shift from controlled laboratory trials to ongoing, real-world affect monitoring'. Use 2 (§Aligning Asynchronous Modalities, l.145) 'How well a fused model performs depends on how that gap is handled' where the gap is differing sampling rates — supported by §E Multimodal Feature Alignment and by §1 Temporal Synchronisation, which gives the same disparate-rate example (audio 16 kHz, video 30 fps, EEG 128 Hz) and states misalignment impairs classifier performance. Use 3 (§Combining Sensors, l.172) 'Recent surveys add transformer-based architectures and multimodal representation learning as the field's emerging direction' — supported verbatim by the abstract's final sentence. The only residual nit is the plural 'Recent surveys' against a single citation. The prior WEAK was recorded against an older sentence ('maximum accuracy in controlled labs where participants sit still'), which has since been rewritten to the narrower claim; the rewrite lands inside what the paper says.
Kumar2025.says: For physiological signals, we emphasize wearable sensing technologies and their transition from controlled laboratory setups to real-world, continuous monitoring. The survey further explores fusion strategies, real-time inference challenges, and emerging directions such as transformer-based architectures and multimodal representation learning. ... In MER, features from many modalities—such as auditory, visual, physiological, and textual—are frequently acquired asynchronously or at disparate sampling rates. Feature alignment guarantees that related data segments across modalities reflect the same temporal and contextual emotional state, facilitating significant fusion and joint modelling [166]. ... Effective feature alignment is essential for multimodal fusion techniques, as misalignment can cause temporal drift, diminish semantic coherence, and impair classifier performance.

Yannakakis2018.label: Yannakakis et al., 2018
Yannakakis2018.full: Yannakakis, G. N., Cowie, R., and Busso, C. (2018). The ordinal nature of emotions: An emerging approach. IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing.
Yannakakis2018.note: Found the quoted phrase verbatim in the local PDF text (downloaded_by_author/Yannakakis_OrdinalNature.txt); the thesis's 'Treating annotation traces this way' correctly stands in for the paper's 'second-order processing of annotation traces as ordinal data'. Fully supported.
Yannakakis2018.says: With this empirical evidence at hand it is safe to conclude that the second-order processing of annotation traces as ordinal data not only yields more valid but also more general models of affect.

Singh2026.label: Singh et al., 2026
Singh2026.full: Singh, L., Georgara, A., Deshmukh, J., Nguyen, T. V. T., and Ramchurn, S. D. (2026). Decision-level fusion for robust wearable affect recognition. arXiv preprint arXiv:2605.14878.
Singh2026.note: The single remaining use is a statement of how the published rule differs from weighting each sensor by its own validation score, and it is exactly right. Eq. 14 is P_T(e) = (1/gamma) * sum_i (1 - H(P_i))^{F1_i} * P_i(e): the per-instance predictive entropy is the base and the sensor's F1 is only the exponent, and the paper itself says the rule prioritises 'primarily according to the entropy, and secondly according to the confidence score', with the entropy instance-specific and F1 'descriptive of the SSP in general'. The earlier WEAK verdict was aimed at a version of the text that credited the paper with per-sensor validation weighting; that text is gone and the sentence now in the thesis states the difference the audit asked for. Residual scope facts worth keeping in the surrounding prose if they are not already there: three-class classification on WESAD (15 subjects; ECG, EDA, BVP, EMG, ACC) scored by accuracy/F1, and the authors call it 'preliminary evaluation' in a short workshop paper, not continuous affect scored by CCC. No repair needed to this sentence.
Singh2026.says: Notably, the entropy is predicted-instance specific, while the confidence score is descriptive of the SSP in general. As such, using the entropy as the base and the confidence score as the power, we regulate the influence of each individual decision, prioritising primarily according to the entropy, and secondly according to the confidence score.

MarinMoreales2018.label: Marín-Morales et al., 2018
MarinMoreales2018.full: Marín-Morales, J., Higuera-Trujillo, J. L., Greco, A., Guixeres, J., Llinares, C., Scilingo, E. P., Alcañiz, M., and Valenza, G. (2018). Affective computing in virtual reality: Emotion recognition from brain and heartbeat dynamics using wearable sensors. Scientific Reports.
MarinMoreales2018.note: MarinMoreales2018 Intro §1.2, last sentence Affective computing taken into VR, recognising emotion from wearable brain and cardiac signals Marín-Morales et al. (2018), Scientific Reports . EEG + ECG from 60 participants in four immersive virtual rooms designed to elicit each quadrant of the circumplex; SVM on brain and cardiac dynamics, 75.00% arousal / 71.21% valence. OK — exactly the claim. Note it is not one of the "standard datasets"; it is cited separately and correctly fulltext, 2026-09-01

MarinMorales2019.label: Marín-Morales et al., 2019
MarinMorales2019.full: Marín-Morales, J., Higuera-Trujillo, J. L., Greco, A., Guixeres, J., Llinares, C., Scilingo, E. P., Alcañiz, M., and Valenza, G. (2019). Real vs. immersive-virtual emotional experience: analysis of psycho-physiological patterns in a free exploration of an art museum. PLoS ONE, 14(10):e0223881.
MarinMorales2019.note: The cohort figure (15 of 60 rejected) and the protocol (LOSO) match. Two errors in the citing sentence were corrected on 2026-09-21: the axes were named in the wrong order, since 71.52 and 75.00 are arousal and 77.08 and 71.08 are valence, and the virtual valence figure was written as 71.05 where the paper reports 71.08. Checked against the open-access PLoS ONE article.
MarinMorales2019.says: Data from 15 subjects out of 60 were rejected due to poor quality. Trigeorgis2016.label: Trigeorgis et al., 2016
Trigeorgis2016.full: Trigeorgis, G., Nicolaou, M. A., Schuller, B. W., and Zafeiriou, S. (2016). Deep canonical time warping. Proceedings of the IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR).
Trigeorgis2016.note: Both remaining uses are accurate. 'Aligning Asynchronous Modalities': the paper's objective is a single argmin over the network parameters theta_1, theta_2 AND the warping matrices Delta_1, Delta_2 (Eq. 11), so 'learns new features and a warping of the timeline jointly' is right, and 'both maximally correlated and temporally aligned' is the paper's own phrasing. The earlier WEAK was against the wording 'stretches the timeline and, at the same time, learns new features'; the current 'jointly' is correct for a joint objective even though the solver alternates ('Clearly, the objective can be solved via alternating optimisation'), so no change is needed. 'Alignment Method Comparison': DCTW is precisely DCCA plus the warping step, stated by the paper itself (setting Delta_i = I reduces Eq. 14 to the DCCA objective), so describing the thesis arms as correlated projections and then those projections plus warping is correct. One scope caveat worth knowing but not worth a citation change: every DCTW experiment in the paper aligns recordings of one and the same event (Weizmann actions, facial-expression video pairs, simultaneous acoustic and articulatory XRMB recordings, CUAVE audio-visual utterances), never physiologically distinct sensor streams; the thesis sentences only describe what the method does, so they do not depend on that. The pupil/skin-conductance illustration the earlier audit flagged no longer appears in any sentence citing this key.
Trigeorgis2016.says: we propose Deep Canonical Time Warping (DCTW), a novel method aimed towards the alignment of multiple sequences that discovers complex, hierarchical representations which are both maximally correlated and temporally aligned. [...] The goal of Deep Canonical Time Warping (DCTW) is to discover a hierarchical non-linear representation of the data sets Xi, i = {1, 2} where the transformed features are (i) temporally aligned with each other, and (ii) maximally correlated. [...] Note that by setting Delta_i = I, Eq. 14 becomes an objective for learning transformations for multiple sequences via DCCA [2].

A 374: 20150176; the key is misnamed Valenza2014 but the bibliography entry and the paper match) states both halves of the thesis sentence in its own abstract and repeats them in the discussion: the valence signature in brain-heart coupling is strongest at intermediate arousing levels, and rising arousal mitigates or washes out the valence effect entirely by arousal level 4. Minor tension to be aware of: the discussion notes valence differences are also visible at the lowest arousal level, so 'clearest at intermediate arousal' follows the paper's abstract rather than every detail of figure 4. [...] MIC differences between negative and positive valence (figure 4), which are visible at the lowest level of arousal (i.e. arousal level 1), changed both in sign and in spatial location at higher levels of arousal (level 2 and 3) and disappear at the highest level of arousal (level 4). [...] increasing arousing elicitations seems to mitigate, or even to washout, the impact of valence on brain-heart dynamics in response to visual elicitation.

Cohen1968.label: Cohen, 1968
Cohen1968.full: Cohen, J. (1968). Weighted kappa: nominal scale agreement provision for scaled disagreement or partial credit. Psychological Bulletin, 70(4), 213--220. DOI 10.1037/h0026256.
Cohen1968.note: The prior verdict was formed without the paper. The full 1968 article (found locally as literature/downloaded_by_author/h0026256.txt, the scanned Psychological Bulletin 70(4):213-220 original) prints the squared-distance weight matrix explicitly, in words and as a 5x5 table, and restates it in prose as weighting disagreements 'proportional to the square of the distance between the pair of measures'. Both thesis sentences say exactly that and nothing more, so both are supported by the primary source. Cohen does present the quadratic pattern as one admissible choice among user-selected weights (he introduces it in the section showing kappa_w = r under equal marginals), so Cohen 1968 is the right citation for WHAT quadratic weighting is; Fleiss and Cohen (1973) is needed only if the thesis additionally claims the equivalence between quadratic-weighted kappa and the intraclass correlation, which neither of these two sentences does. Adding Fleiss and Cohen 1973 here would be harmless but is not required, and the prior auditor's charge of over-attribution does not survive contact with the paper.
Cohen1968.says: It means that r can be conceived as a (suitably chance-corrected) proportion of agreement, where the disagreements are weighted so as to be proportional to the square of the distance between the pair of measures, or, equivalently, from the X = Y line. ... (b) Disagreement weights (v_ij) are assigned according to the following pattern: The k cells of the agreement diagonal (i = j) have v_ij = 0. The k - 1 cells in each of the two adjacent diagonals have v_ij of 1, the k - 2 cells in each of the next diagonals out on either side have v_ij = 2^2 = 4, the k - 3 cells in each of the next diagonals have v_ij = 3^2 = 9, and so on until one reaches the last cell in the upper right and lower left corner whose weights are (k - 1)^2. For example, for k = 5, the pattern of v_ij is / 0 1 4 9 16 / 1 0 1 4 9 / 4 1 0 1 4 / 9 4 1 0 1 / 16 9 4 1 0 /

Stuldreher2023.says: Individuals that pay attention to narrative stimuli show synchronized heart rate (HR) and electrodermal activity (EDA) responses. The degree to which this physiological synchrony occurs is related to attentional engagement.

Specker2020.label: Specker et al., 2020
Specker2020.full: Specker, E., Forster, M., Brinkmann, H., Boddy, J., Immelmann, B., Goller, J., Pelowski, M., Rosenberg, R., and Leder, H. (2020). Warm, lively, rough? Assessing agreement on aesthetic effects of artworks. PLoS ONE, 15(5), e0232083.
Specker2020.note: Read the full abstract via Europe PMC. 'Responses to art are only partly shared' is precisely the paper's finding - agreement on 3 of 14 aesthetic-effect dimensions, and lowest on the evaluative ones closest to valence. Stimuli are abstract artworks and their extracted lines/colours rather than a museum, and the measure is rating agreement rather than physiology, but the thesis uses it only for the rating-agreement point, which is fair.
Specker2020.says: In one study and its replication, we found significantly lower agreement than expected. For the whole artworks, participants agreed on the effects of warm-cold, heavy-light, and happy-sad, but not on 11 other dimensions. ... agreement was especially low on dimensions usually of interest in empirical aesthetics (e.g., like-dislike).

Szymanska2025.label: Szymańska et al., 2025
Szymanska2025.full: Szymańska, A., Jemioło, P., Pacuła-Leśniak, B., and Kuniecki, M. (2025). Pupil-Based Prediction of Affect in VR: A Machine Learning Approach. 2025 IEEE Conference on Virtual Reality and 3D User Interfaces Abstracts and Workshops (VRW), 1376--1377. doi:10.1109/VRW66409.2025.00334.
Szymanska2025.note: Szymanska2025 [69] §2.3 pupil para F1 0.73 arousal / 0.64 valence binary, but only 0.31 / 0.28 at nine levels; no subject-independent evaluation reported Two-page abstract. 105 participants (50 men, 55 women) viewing luminance-matched emotional images in a headset; LightGBM on pupil and gaze features; binary, 9-level multiclass and regression tasks. The closest precedent to this thesis's sensor and setting, and evidence that pupil-based prediction degrades sharply with target granularity. OK (after rewrite) fulltext, 2026-09-02

GutierrezMartin2024.label: Gutiérrez-Martín et al., 2024
GutierrezMartin2024.full: Gutiérrez-Martín, L., López-Ongil, C., Lanza-Gutiérrez, J. M., and Miranda Calero, J. A. (2024). Personalized clustering for emotion recognition improvement. Sensors, 24(24), 8110.
GutierrezMartin2024.note: Verified the published abstract (Crossref for 10.3390/s24248110) plus the PMC full text: 44 participants in an immersive VR violence-elicitation task, wearable GSR/skin temperature/BVP, hierarchical clustering of subjects with a stated procedure for enrolling new unlabelled users into a cluster. Good modality and scale fit, and it supports all three uses including the future-work suggestion that personalisation could start from a cluster.
GutierrezMartin2024.says: These semi-personalized models will be applicable to clusters of subjects sharing similarities in their emotional reactions to external stimuli. ... Experimental results demonstrate an improvement of 5% in accuracy and 4% in F1 score with respect to our baseline general model, along with a 32% to 58% reduction in variability, respectively.

Tukey1977.label: Tukey, 1977
Tukey1977.full: Tukey, J. W. (1977). Exploratory Data Analysis. Addison-Wesley, Reading, MA.
Tukey1977.note: The book itself was not available locally; the quotation above (p.3) is corroborated across independent quotation collections, and Tukey is the canonical source for both the EDA-first principle and the exploratory/confirmatory split, so both uses stand. Minor wording issue in the thesis, not a citation error: Tukey's point is that exploration suggests hypotheses which a separate confirmatory step then tests, whereas 'each hypothesis is tested against the data before any confirmatory step' reads as if testing happens inside EDA.
Tukey1977.says: Exploratory data analysis can never be the whole story, but nothing else can serve as the foundation stone - as the first step.

Trondle2012.label: Tröndle and Tschacher, 2012
Trondle2012.full: Tröndle, M. and Tschacher, W. (2012). The physiology of phenomenology: The effects of artworks. Empirical Studies of the Arts, 30(1), 75--113. DOI 10.2190/EM.30.1.g.
Trondle2012.note: Trondle2012 Intro §1.1 ¶1, sentence 2 Emotional responses leave measurable traces in the body, grounded in a gallery Tröndle & Tschacher (2012), Empirical Studies of the Arts 30(1), 75–113. The eMotion project: visitor locomotion plus continuous cardiac measures and skin-conductance variability plus subjective assessment, in a working gallery. First evidence that aesthetic response can be statistically grounded in viewers' physiology in an ecologically valid setting. OK abstract, 2026-09-01

SunSaenko2016CORAL.label: Sun et al., 2016
SunSaenko2016CORAL.full: Sun, B., Feng, J., and Saenko, K. (2016). Return of frustratingly easy domain adaptation. Proceedings of the Thirtieth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, 2058--2065.
SunSaenko2016CORAL.note: Read the local text: the method whitens source features and re-colours them with the target covariance, has an analytical (closed-form) solution, and needs no target labels and no retraining — matching both thesis sentences. It is a vision/NLP paper, but CORAL is a generic feature-space transform, so per-participant use is a legitimate application rather than an overreach.
SunSaenko2016CORAL.says: CORAL minimizes domain shift by aligning the second-order statistics of source and target distributions, without requiring any target labels.

SalvucciGoldberg2000.label: Salvucci and Goldberg, 2000
SalvucciGoldberg2000.full: Salvucci, D. D. and Goldberg, J. H. (2000). Identifying fixations and saccades in eye-tracking protocols. In Proceedings of the 2000 Symposium on Eye Tracking Research \& Applications (ETRA), 71--78. DOI 10.1145/355017.355028.
SalvucciGoldberg2000.note: SalvucciGoldberg2000 [73] §2.3 pupil para A taxonomy of five fixation-identification algorithms; I-VT is the velocity-threshold member Proposes a taxonomy of fixation-identification algorithms and describes five: I-VT, I-HMM, I-DT, I-MST, I-AOI, across velocity-based, dispersion-based and area-based families. The definition of I-VT, and the fact that the choice of algorithm is unsettled. OK (after rewrite) fulltext, 2026-09-02

Ke2017.label: Ke et al., 2017
Ke2017.full: Ke, G., Meng, Q., Finley, T., Wang, T., Chen, W., Ma, W., Ye, Q., and Liu, T.-Y. (2017). LightGBM: A highly efficient gradient boosting decision tree. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS), 30, 3146--3154.
Ke2017.note: Read the NeurIPS PDF; LightGBM is explicitly presented as a GBDT implementation, which is all the thesis's sentence ('GBT is realised as XGBoost or LightGBM') requires. Correct and minimal use.
Ke2017.says: We call our new GBDT implementation with GOSS and EFB LightGBM. Our experiments on multiple public datasets show that LightGBM can accelerate the training process by up to over 20 times while achieving almost the same accuracy.

Elgendi2013.label: Elgendi et al., 2013
Elgendi2013.full: Elgendi, M., Norton, I., Brearley, M., Abbott, D., and Schuurmans, D. (2013). Systolic peak detection in acceleration photoplethysmograms measured from emergency responders in tropical conditions. PLoS ONE, 8(10), e76585. DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0076585.
Elgendi2013.note: Repaired. The 99.8 per cent figure covers all 160 recordings, three quarters of them taken after exercise in tropical heat, not rest alone. The sentence now says so, which is both accurate and closer to a moving visitor than rest would be.
Elgendi2013.says: With 40 healthy subjects, the new algorithm demonstrates the highest overall detection accuracy (99.84% sensitivity, 99.89% positive predictivity). [...] The algorithms were tested on 40 subjects with PPG signals measured at four time points: before exercise, after exercise 1, after exercise 2, and after exercise 3; with total number of 160 recordings.

Shen2023CLISA.label: Shen et al., 2023
Shen2023CLISA.full: Shen, X., Liu, X., Hu, X., Zhang, D., and Song, S. (2023). Contrastive learning of subject-invariant EEG representations for cross-subject emotion recognition. IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing, 14(3), 2496--2511.
Shen2023CLISA.note: Directly supports the clause it is attached to — that subject-invariant features can be learned by aligning people contrastively. Flag on fit only: it is EEG (80 and 15 subjects) and deep representation learning, i.e. neither this thesis's modality nor its model family, so it is fine as one item in a list of approaches but should not be leaned on as evidence that this would work on wrist EDA/PPG at n=15-22.
Shen2023CLISA.says: Contrastive learning was employed to minimize the inter-subject differences by maximizing the similarity in EEG signal representations across subjects when they received the same emotional stimuli in contrast to different ones.

Luo2024NormWear.label: Luo et al., 2024
Luo2024NormWear.full: Luo, Y., Chen, Y., Salekin, A., and Rahman, T. (2024). Toward foundation model for multivariate wearable sensing of physiological signals. arXiv preprint arXiv:2412.09758.
Luo2024NormWear.note: Exactly supports the claim that pretrained physiological foundation models supply a general-purpose embedding learned from large external corpora rather than from the study's own participants. Good fit: wearable PPG/GSR are the thesis's own modalities, and the paper is cited only for the existence of the approach, not for any performance number.
Luo2024NormWear.says: we propose NORMWEAR, the first multi-modal and ubiquitous foundation model designed to extract generalized and informative representations from wearable sensing data. [...] NORMWEAR is pretrained on a diverse set of physiological signals, including PPG, ECG, EEG, GSR, and IMU, from various public datasets.

Simon2026RAP.label: Simon and Chetouani, 2026
Simon2026RAP.full: Simon, L. and Chetouani, M. (2026). Retrieval-augmented personalization with foundation models for wearable stress detection. arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.24985.
Simon2026RAP.note: This is precisely 'person-specific structure retrieved from the person's own history instead of modelled', and the fit is good: WESAD wrist EDA/BVP/temperature with N=15, the same scale and sensor class as the thesis.
Simon2026RAP.says: Our method leverages frozen, out-of-domain foundation models to retrieve similar patterns from a target user's history and encode them into a compact personalized embedding that modulates representations extracted by a lightweight transformer network.

WuOrdinal2025.label: Wu et al., 2025
WuOrdinal2025.full: Wu, J., Barthet, M., Melhart, D., and Yannakakis, G. N. (2025). Emotions as ambiguity-aware ordinal representations. In Proceedings of the International Conference on Affective Computing and Intelligent Interaction (ACII). arXiv:2508.19193.
WuOrdinal2025.note: The citing sentence matches the abstract exactly, including the bounded/unbounded contrast the thesis then draws on. Good fit: continuous affect traces, CCC as the metric, RECOLA and GameVibe — the same problem shape as the thesis, even though the models are LSTMs rather than tree ensembles.
WuOrdinal2025.says: Our results demonstrate that ordinal representations outperform conventional ambiguity-aware models on unbounded labels, achieving the highest Concordance Correlation Coefficient (CCC) and Signed Differential Agreement (SDA) scores, highlighting their effectiveness in modeling the traces' dynamics. For bounded traces, ordinal representations excel in SDA.

Mitsios2024.label: Mitsios et al., 2024
Mitsios2024.full: Mitsios, M. et al. (2024). Improved text emotion prediction using combined valence and arousal ordinal classification. Proceedings of the 2024 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 2: Short Papers), 808--813.
Mitsios2024.note: Repaired. The clause equating their discretisation with this thesis's is gone: their labels are categorical emotion words ordered along valence and arousal, not binned continuous traces. The quotation about unequal misclassification costs stands.
Mitsios2024.says: We argue that not all misclassifications are of the same importance, as there are perceptual similarities among emotional classes. We thus redefine the emotion labeling problem by shifting it from a traditional classification model to an ordinal classification one, where discrete emotions are arranged in a sequential order according to their valence levels.

Lu2023DFFNet.label: Lu et al., 2023
Lu2023DFFNet.full: Lu, W., Liu, H., Ma, H., Tan, T.-P., and Xia, L. (2023). Hybrid transfer learning strategy for cross-subject EEG emotion recognition. Frontiers in Human Neuroscience, 17:1280241. DOI 10.3389/fnhum.2023.1280241.
Lu2023DFFNet.note: Checked the local PDF text: the thesis's 93.4% and 82.3% round 93.37% and 82.32% correctly, the two benchmarks (SEED, SEED-IV) are indeed established, and the method is domain adaptation plus few-shot fine-tuning as described. The thesis is also explicit that these are EEG and categorical rather than dimensional targets, which is the right hedge for a wearable-sensor thesis.
Lu2023DFFNet.says: The proposed DFF-Net surpasses the state-of-the-art methods in the cross-subject EEG emotion recognition task, achieving an average recognition accuracy of 93.37% on the SEED dataset and 82.32% on the SEED-IV dataset.

BenedekDeconv2010.label: Benedek and Kaernbach, 2010
BenedekDeconv2010.full: Benedek, M. and Kaernbach, C. (2010). Decomposition of skin conductance data by means of nonnegative deconvolution. Psychophysiology, 47(4), 647--658.
BenedekDeconv2010.note: Repaired. The sentence claimed 0.01 to 0.05 microsiemens was the size of a single skin-conductance response; the paper gives it as the conventional minimum for counting one at all. Reworded to say that, which is what the quotation supports and what the 0.02 microsiemens exclusion rule actually rests on.
BenedekDeconv2010.says: Conventionally, SCRs that arise within a predefined response window (1–3 s to 1–5 s after stimulus onset) and that also meet a minimum amplitude criterion (0.01 to 0.05 μS) are considered to be elicited by the stimulus ( Dawson et al., 2007 ; Levinson & Edelberg, 1985 ). ... Impulses occurred with a mean onset latency of 1249 ms ( SD =246.4) and a mean peak latency of 2095 ms ( SD =308.8). They showed a mean duration of 1615 ms ( SD =416.8) ... PO components showed a mean duration of 4296 ms ( SD =1045.3) ... Their mean peak latency was 3573 ms ( SD =573.3).

Bhatti2022.label: Hossain et al., 2022
Bhatti2022.full: Hossain, M.-B., Kong, Y., Posada-Quintero, H. F., and Chon, K. H. (2022). Comparison of electrodermal activity from multiple body locations based on standard EDA indices' quality and robustness against motion artifact. Sensors, 22(9), 3177.
Bhatti2022.note: Repaired. The wrist was never among the sites compared, and the motion finding favours the forehead, not the finger. The sentence now says which four sites were compared, that the wrist was not one of them, and separates the signal-quality result from the motion result.
Bhatti2022.says: We also evaluated the robustness of the different body sites against motion artifacts and found that the foot EDA location was the best alternative to other sites. ... As can be seen from Figure 4, the forehead is the most robust site against motion artifacts, as evidenced by the relatively low spectral power in the noise band compared to other measurement sites.

BoucseinSPR2012.label: Boucsein et al., 2012
BoucseinSPR2012.full: Boucsein, W., Fowles, D. C., Grimnes, S., Ben-Shakhar, G., Roth, W. T., Dawson, M. E., and Filion, D. L. (2012). Publication recommendations for electrodermal measurements. Psychophysiology, 49(8), 1017--1034.
BoucseinSPR2012.note: Could not open the full text (Wiley 403, BIOPAC mirror 403), but the abstract confirmed on three independent pages (PubMed record, Hebrew University CRIS, Semantic Scholar) establishes this is the SPR committee report on EDA recording and reporting, which is exactly the load the thesis sentence puts on it. Verified from abstract only, not full text.
BoucseinSPR2012.says: This committee was appointed by the SPR Board to provide recommendations for publishing data on electrodermal activity (EDA).

Castaldo2019.label: Castaldo et al., 2019
Castaldo2019.full: Castaldo, R., Montesinos, L., Melillo, P., James, C., and Pecchia, L. (2019). Ultra-short term HRV features as surrogates of short term HRV: a case study on mental stress detection in real life. BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making, 19, 12.
Castaldo2019.note: The six-of-23 count and the identity of the omitted pair are exact: MeanHR and StdHR are the heart-rate restatements of MeanNN and StdNN, leaving MeanNN, SDNN, HF and SD2. One nuance for the window sentence: the paper found three of the six (MeanNN, StdHR, HF) still usable at 30 s, so sixty seconds is the floor for the index set the thesis uses rather than for HRV indices in general; also note the paper's data are ECG at rest versus a mental-arithmetic stressor, not wrist PPG during walking.
Castaldo2019.says: Six out of 23 ultra-short HRV features (MeanNN, StdNN, MeanHR, StdHR, HF, and SD2) displayed consistency across all of the excerpt lengths (i.e., from 5 to 1 min).

Hinde2025.label: Coste et al., 2025
Hinde2025.full: Coste, A., Millour, G., and Hausswirth, C. (2025). A comparative study between ECG- and PPG-based heart rate sensors for heart rate variability measurements: influence of body position, duration, sex, and age. Sensors, 25(18), 5745.
Hinde2025.note: Verified from the open-access PMC full text (Coste, Millour and Hausswirth, Sensors 2025): validation covered only supine and seated rest ('Testing was conducted on a massage table for the supine position and a comfortable office chair for the seated position'), with no movement or ambulatory condition, so the thesis is right that walking wrist recordings sit outside it and that optical sensors yield PRV. Note the key name 'Hinde2025' does not match the Coste et al. entry — a leftover label worth fixing.
Hinde2025.says: PPG-derived HRV—often referred to as pulse rate variability (PRV)—may differ from ECG-derived HRV due to variations in pulse wave propagation.

Kelbsch2019.label: Kelbsch et al., 2019
Kelbsch2019.full: Kelbsch, C., Strasser, T., Chen, Y., Feigl, B., Gamlin, P. D., Kardon, R., et al. (2019). Standards in pupillography. Frontiers in Neurology, 10, 129.
Kelbsch2019.note: All three uses check out: the standards do ask for background/room illuminance to be reported, and the paper explicitly attributes pupil dilation to cognitive/effortful/emotional stimulation as well as to light. It is a clinical-pupillography standards document, so it is being used for a general methodological point rather than for anything about VR or affect prediction, which is a legitimate use.
Kelbsch2019.says: We recommend to report the background and room illuminance (Lux) during the measurements and, if applicable, the pre-dark or pre–light adaptation times to room illumination (light-adapted vs. dark-adapted vs. mesopic condition vs. no adaptation). [...] Dilation in response to cognitive, effortful or emotional stimulation is mediated by both direct activation of the sympathetic system on dilator muscles of the iris, and by inhibition of the [parasympathetic pathway].

Kuijpers2022.label: Kuhn et al., 2022
Kuijpers2022.full: Kuhn, M., Gerlicher, A. M. V., and Lonsdorf, T. B. (2022). Navigating the manyverse of skin conductance response quantification approaches -- a direct comparison of trough-to-peak, baseline-corrected, and model-based approaches. Psychophysiology, 59, e14058.
Kuijpers2022.note: Verified the published abstract (Crossref for 10.1111/psyp.14058). The count of seven and the 'none universally best' conclusion are exact. Fit caveat worth a clause in the thesis: the seven approaches are event-related SCR scoring methods (two trough-to-peak raters, script baseline correction, Ledalab, four PsPM models) on fear-conditioning data, and do not include either cvxEDA or a frequency split, so the paper licenses the general 'search it' argument but not a comparison of the thesis's two specific decompositions.
Kuijpers2022.says: Our results from seven different SCR quantification approaches applied to two data sets with different paradigms suggest that there may be no single approach that consistently yields larger effect sizes and could be universally considered "best." Yet, at least some of the approaches employed show consistent effect sizes within each data set indicating comparability.

Laborde2017.label: Laborde et al., 2017
Laborde2017.full: Laborde, S., Mosley, E., and Thayer, J. F. (2017). Heart rate variability and cardiac vagal tone in psychophysiological research: recommendations for experiment planning, data analysis, and data reporting. Frontiers in Psychology, 8, 213.
Laborde2017.note: Found the exact sentence in the local full text; the thesis's 'even a ten-second record yields a valid value' for RMSSD is a faithful paraphrase. Worth noting the paper's own hedge that averaging several 10 s windows is preferable, and that the finding is reported from Munoz et al. (N = 3,387) rather than original data.
Laborde2017.says: In addition, even a single 10 s (standard ECG) was found to yield a valid RMSSD measurement, although an average over multiple 10 s ECGs is preferable.

LlanesJurado2020.label: Llanes-Jurado et al., 2020
LlanesJurado2020.full: Llanes-Jurado, J., Marín-Morales, J., Guixeres, J., and Alcañiz, M. (2020). Development and calibration of an eye-tracking fixation identification algorithm for immersive virtual reality. Sensors, 20(17), 4956.
LlanesJurado2020.note: A .txt of this paper does exist locally despite the batch record listing no copy. The 1 degree / 0.25 s optimum, the headset (HTC Vive Pro Eye with integrated 120 Hz eye tracking), and the stationary caveat all check out: participants stood at a fixed marked position and looked at lit panels, moving the head but not locomoting.
LlanesJurado2020.says: The results show that distance-dispersion thresholds between 1-1.6 degrees and time windows between 0.25-0.4 s are the acceptable range parameters, with 1 degree and 0.25 s being the optimum.

Charlton2022PPG.label: Charlton et al., 2022
Charlton2022PPG.full: Charlton, P. H., Kyriacou, P. A., Mant, J., Marozas, V., Chowienczyk, P., and Alastruey, J. (2022). Wearable photoplethysmography for cardiovascular monitoring. Proceedings of the IEEE, 110(3), 355--381.
Charlton2022PPG.note: A local .txt exists despite local_copy being null in the batch; the review states plainly that accelerometry is a standard reference signal for motion-artifact removal in wearable PPG, which is exactly what the thesis says. Good fit for a wrist-PPG thesis.
Charlton2022PPG.says: Reference motion signals that can be used include accelerometry [81], [82], the gyroscope signal [83], or a PPG signal of a different wavelength (such as using an infrared PPG to remove motion artifact from a green PPG) [84].

LipponenTarvainen2019.label: Lipponen and Tarvainen, 2019
LipponenTarvainen2019.full: Lipponen, J. A. and Tarvainen, M. P. (2019). A robust algorithm for heart rate variability time series artefact correction using novel beat classification. Journal of Medical Engineering \& Technology, 43(3), 173--181.
LipponenTarvainen2019.note: Retrieved and read the full PDF from the web: the successive-difference series with a time-varying threshold is exactly the paper's Th1, and the paper fixes its own window (91 beats) and multiplier (a = 5.2), so the thesis's careful statement that 'the window and the multiplier are our own' is both accurate and correctly scoped.
LipponenTarvainen2019.says: To ensure adaptation to different HRV levels, the threshold is estimated from the time-varying distribution of the dRRs series. Th1 is defined as a times quartile deviation (QD) of the 91 surrounding beat interval differences.

LlanesJurado2021.label: Llanes-Jurado et al., 2023
LlanesJurado2021.full: Llanes-Jurado, J., Carrasco-Ribelles, L. A., Alcañiz, M., Soria-Olivas, E., and Marín-Morales, J. (2023). Automatic artifact recognition and correction for electrodermal activity based on LSTM-CNN models. Expert Systems with Applications, 230, 120581.
LlanesJurado2021.note: Could not open the ScienceDirect page (403), so verified via Europe PMC's full abstract of the companion/earlier version 'Automatic Artifact Recognition and Correction for Electrodermal Activity in Uncontrolled Environments' (VR contexts 'in which users can freely walk and move their hands'), and corroborated the same phasic finding for the 2023 ESWA LSTM-CNN paper (43 subjects, 74 h, EDABE benchmark). The thesis claim - automated correction matches manual expert cleaning at the phasic level in free-moving immersive VR - is exactly what the paper reports. Minor housekeeping: the key says 2021 while the bibliography entry is the 2023 ESWA paper; pick one version.
LlanesJurado2021.says: The data from 44 subjects during an immersive VR task were collected and cleaned by two experts as ground truth. ... The evaluation of this correction showed that the automatically and manually corrected signals did not present differences in terms of phasic components, while both showed differences to the raw signal.

NystromHolmqvist2010.label: Nyström and Holmqvist, 2010
NystromHolmqvist2010.full: Nyström, M. and Holmqvist, K. (2010). An adaptive algorithm for fixation, saccade, and glissade detection in eyetracking data. Behavior Research Methods, 42(1), 188--204.
NystromHolmqvist2010.note: Repaired. The sentence credited this paper with a median-based threshold; it uses the mean plus six standard deviations, iterated. It now carries only the adaptive iterative estimate, and the median-based robustness is credited to Voloh2020, whose contribution that is.
NystromHolmqvist2010.says: The iterative algorithm is given an initial peak velocity detection threshold PT1, which could be in the range 100 deg - 300 deg/sec, but the choice is not critical as long as there are saccades with peak velocities reaching this threshold. For all samples with velocities lower than PT1, the average (mu) and standard deviation (sigma) are calculated. The threshold is updated as PTn = mu(n-1) + 6*sigma(n-1) for each iteration. ... The iterative process is continued until |PTn - PT(n-1)| is smaller than 1 deg/sec, and PTn is selected as the final velocity threshold. This iteration can be done separately for each participant or even for each trial.

PeterschDierkes2021.label: Petersch and Dierkes, 2022
PeterschDierkes2021.full: Petersch, B. and Dierkes, K. (2022). Gaze-angle dependency of pupil-size measurements in head-mounted eye tracking. Behavior Research Methods, 54(2), 763--779.
PeterschDierkes2021.note: Verified against the local full text; both halves of the thesis sentence -- the foreshortening error and its being 'on a par with the task-evoked responses themselves' in head-mounted trackers -- are the paper's own words. Excellent fit for an HMD eye-tracking thesis.
PeterschDierkes2021.says: Eyeball rotation in relation to the recording camera as well as optical effects due to refraction at corneal interfaces can, however, induce so-called pupil foreshortening errors (PFE), i.e. systematic gaze-angle dependent changes of apparent pupil size that are on a par with typical response amplitudes. While PFE and options for its correction have been discussed for remote eye trackers, for head-mounted eye trackers such an assessment is still lacking.

Schafer2012.label: Schäfer and Vagedes, 2013
Schafer2012.full: Schäfer, A. and Vagedes, J. (2013). How accurate is pulse rate variability as an estimate of heart rate variability? A review on studies comparing photoplethysmographic technology with an electrocardiogram. International Journal of Cardiology, 166(1), 15--29.
Schafer2012.note: Retrieved the abstract through the Europe PMC API (PMID 22809539); it supports the thesis sentence and in fact states the point more strongly, since walking is exactly the physical-activity condition under which the review says agreement degrades unacceptably. Worth noting the bibliography year should be 2013 (Int J Cardiol 166(1):15-29), which the entry already has even though the key says 2012.
Schafer2012.says: Results speak in favor of sufficient accuracy when subjects are at rest, although many studies suggest that short-term variability is somewhat overestimated by PRV... Physical activity and some mental stressors seem to impair the agreement of PRV and HRV, often to an inacceptable extent.

Shaffer2017.label: Shaffer and Ginsberg, 2017
Shaffer2017.full: Shaffer, F. and Ginsberg, J. P. (2017). An overview of heart rate variability metrics and norms. Frontiers in Public Health, 5, 258.
Shaffer2017.note: Both citing sentences check out against the local full text: the three-family taxonomy is the paper's organising scheme and its Table 3 of non-linear measures is Poincare-derived (S, SD1, SD2), and the 2-minute LF and 5-minute VLF minimums are stated verbatim, matching the thesis's 'two and five minutes' exactly.
Shaffer2017.says: We can describe 24 h, short-term (ST, ~5 min) or brief, and ultra-short-term (UST, <5 min) HRV using time-domain, frequency-domain, and non-linear measurements. ... The LF band (0.04-0.15 Hz) is typically recorded over a minimum 2 min period. ... The VLF band (0.0033-0.04 Hz) requires a recording period of at least 5 min, but may be best monitored over 24 h.

Stuart2014.label: Stuart et al., 2014
Stuart2014.full: Stuart, S., Galna, B., Lord, S., Rochester, L., and Godfrey, A. (2014). Quantifying saccades while walking: validity of a novel velocity-based algorithm for mobile eye tracking. Proceedings of the 36th Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC), 5739--5742.
Stuart2014.note: Repaired. The 30 degrees per second seated criterion is not in this paper and has moved to Olsen2012IVT, which states it as the I-VT default. This paper now carries only the 240 degrees per second walking threshold, which it validates.
Stuart2014.says: Following calculation of velocities and accelerations for each frame in the raw data the algorithm then classified each point above a certain velocity threshold (i.e. >240 deg/sec (5 deg)) as a saccade. ... This threshold was used to rule out most of the intrusions from other eye movements and provide purposeful eye movement data which was adaptable depending upon the task (i.e. lower threshold for static tasks). ... appendix.lead:
\chapter{Declaration on the Use of Generative AI}
\label{app:alt-ai-use}

appendix.body: Three generative AI tools were used in preparing this thesis: Claude, ChatGPT and NotebookLM. This declaration records what each was used for.

The work followed a hybrid approach, with the model serving as a partner in discussion. An idea or a problem was put to it, the options were discussed, something was tried, and the result was brought back for further discussion, over many iterations. Ideas moved in both directions, and what stands in this thesis is what survived that exchange and the author's own judgement of it.

ChatGPT was used as a conversational aid to understanding: to talk through a topic or a concept, to ask questions about the field and about methods, and to test the author's own understanding in extended exchanges.

NotebookLM was used during the literature phase to work through individual research papers: to locate the passages relevant to a question, to have a paper's method and findings explained, and to compare what several papers say on the same point.

Every choice the methodology makes, what was carried, what it was carried over, and the
margin the comparison was resolved at. A blank span means the candidates were not scored
against one another on a single number, either because the choice was fixed by a rule rather
than by a score or because the comparison is reported per slice in the chapter itself. A
selection made inside its margin is a convenience among candidates this cohort cannot
distinguish, not a claim that the carried one is better.
